worlds.label: The opening world
worlds.description: Where the film opens: Ben wakes in the house with the three locks on the door. The woman falls through the roof of the car here, and the woman of this world dies in that fall.

worlds.label: The world with her - already running
worlds.description: A world that was already living before Ben arrives in it. The woman he finds at the door here is not the one who fell in his own world.

worlds.label: The world where he died - already running
worlds.description: A world in which the man we follow had already died. It was running before he got there, and it keeps running after he leaves it.

worlds.label: The family world - already running
worlds.description: A world where the family is whole: the boy rides in the car. The man who comes back from the cabin is cruel there, which the script implies and never shows.

worlds.label: He dies at the shot in the storm
worlds.description: The other half of the split: in this world the shot kills him. It carries on without him.

worlds.label: He dies at the shot in the cabin
worlds.description: The other half of the split: in this world the shot kills him. It carries on without him.

worlds.label: He dies at the last shot
worlds.description: The other half of the last split: in this world he dies of the shot he fires into his own mouth. It carries on without him.

worlds.label: The other half of the crash
worlds.description: The crash splits the world in two. The film follows one half - the one where the boy dies in the car; the other half is never shown.

agents.label: Ben (opening world)
agents.notes: Carries nothing from one world into the next: he does not remember the fall, the cabin or the shots.

agents.label: The Waif
agents.notes: The same woman in every world, and the only one who remembers between them. She has many names - Alice, Mary, Junebug, Kit. She is the one who fell in the opening world, and she wears red-striped shoes.

agents.label: The woman who falls (opening world)
agents.notes: The woman of the opening world, who jumps from the office window and dies on the roof of the car. The woman Ben meets afterwards is not her.

agents.label: Marie
agents.notes: Ben's partner. Dies in the siege in the world where he died; alive in the family world.

agents.label: Jack
agents.notes: Ben's son. Killed in the crash - his head is cut through, the way his mother is cut through by the bone in her thigh.

agents.label: The Others
agents.notes: Pale-fire figures that have to be looked at to exist. They take the woman apart at the end of a pass and light her up again.

agents.label: Q. R. Preston
agents.notes: Wrote the book about the rules that govern all of this. His revolver is the one in the crawlspace. His address is on the book.

agents.label: Jamie
agents.notes: Wants the cabin, but will not buy it without the permit.

events.label: Ben wakes in the house
events.description: Ben's eyes snap open. He walks the house with a bat, checks the mirror, and throws the three locks on the front door.

events.label: The drive with the family
events.description: Marie writes equations on paper in the passenger seat while Ben drives. Jack is in the car. Ben makes the green light and says he hates this intersection.

events.label: She comes through the roof
events.description: A woman falls from a great height onto the roof of the moving car. The roof comes down on Marie and Jack. This is where the world splits in two.

events.label: The woman of this world dies
events.description: The woman who fell does not survive the fall. She is the woman of this world, and this is the last of her.

events.label: The motel and the courthouse
events.description: Ben lives in a motel. At the courthouse Marie keeps the house and Ben is given the cabin. He says he has accepted that Jack is gone.

events.label: The cabin
events.description: The cabin: a bat hanging, maggots, a window smashed in.

events.label: The book in the cabin
events.description: A book is in the cabin: it is called The Rules of Quantum Immortality, and it was written by Q. R. Preston.

events.label: The revolver in the crawlspace
events.description: A rosewood box under the cabin holds a seven-sided revolver. Six of its chambers fire; the seventh is the one that goes on burning.

events.label: Six cans destroyed
events.description: Ben tries the gun on six cans and destroys all of them. He says it is good enough to know he should not be this good.

events.label: He shoots himself before she arrives
events.description: Ben puts the revolver in his mouth and pulls the trigger, before anyone has arrived at the door. The world splits: one half carries him on, the other half kills him.

events.label: He comes round in a world with her in it
events.description: He comes round in a world that was already running without him - the same cabin, the same night, but in this one the woman is alive and looking for him.

events.label: She arrives at the door
events.description: A soaked young woman stands at the cabin door in the storm. There is broken glass in her foot. She says she was hoping he would remember.

events.label: The blue ball
events.description: She is carrying Jack's blue ball. It is not from this world.

events.label: What happened to her in the padded room
events.description: She remembers being kept in a padded room, and being given the book there. Where the book came from, she never says.

events.label: He shoots himself while she tells him to
events.description: With her urging him on, Ben puts the revolver to himself and fires again. The world splits: in one half he lives, in the other he is dead.

events.label: He comes round in the world where he died
events.description: He comes round in the world his own death already belongs to - a world that had been running without him and keeps its own history.

events.label: The siege: Marie and Jack are killed
events.description: The house is attacked. Marie runs with Jack. The roof of the pickup comes down on them, and Marie is killed and so is the boy - half his head gone, the way it was in the crash.

events.label: The seventh chamber is cut away
events.description: The pale figures will not take Ben: they have to be looked at to exist, and he will not do it. The woman cuts the seventh chamber out of the revolver so it will fire every time.

events.label: She was the one who fell
events.description: She tells him she did not shoot herself - she jumped. Her shoes are the red-striped ones. She was the woman who came through the car roof.

events.label: She asks him to shoot her
events.description: She tells him to put the gun on her and fire, because she is where all of the pain comes from. He refuses her.

events.label: He goes back to the cabin and shoots himself again
events.description: He returns to the cabin and fires into his own mouth rather than at her. He looks at his own death instead of turning away from it. The world splits one last time: he lives on in one half and dies in the other.

payload.note: chart split 184; the shot shown at p113 #266

events.label: The Others take her apart
events.description: The pale figures pull the woman to pieces. She comes back with dead eyes, clicks her fingers, and the pale light goes out.

events.label: He comes round in the world where they are alive
events.description: The last split lands him in a world where Marie and Jack were never taken from him - a world that had been running without him.

events.label: The light stays red
events.description: He is driving with Jack beside him. The light turns red and he stops, and nothing falls out of the sky. They wait.

events.label: Jack draws on the glass
events.description: Jack runs his finger over the glass of the car window. The camera pulls back over the crossroads and the picture goes dark.

events.label: He dies at the shot in the storm
events.description: In this half of the split the shot kills him. The world goes on without him.

events.label: He dies at the shot in the cabin
events.description: In this half of the split the shot kills him. The world goes on without him.

events.label: He dies at the last shot
events.description: In this half of the split the shot into his own mouth kills him. The world goes on without him.

ruleEffects.effect: the fall onto the car is where the world splits; the same fall happens in every world
the woman who falls is the same woman in every world, and she is the only one who remembers between them

interventions.notes: The film's opening act of interference with itself: she is both the cause of the crash and the one who arrives afterwards at the door.

ruleEffects.effect: each shot forks the world: one half carries him on, the other half is finished with him

interventions.notes: The gun does this by itself. He is not choosing a branch; both halves happen.

outcome.summary: The man we follow is carried through one world after another by a gun that splits the world every time it fires, and by a woman who is in all of them and remembers all of them. He ends in a world where the boy is in the car and the light turns red and nothing falls. The film's last picture is that red light; the chart of his story stops one shot earlier, on the shot he fires into his own mouth, because that is where he chose to look at his own death.

semanticReview.note: No rule set in the catalogue states this work's physics: that a death is refused unless it is observed, and that the one who survives comes round in a world that was already running. The nearest catalogue laws (worldline_attractor for the recurring worlds and the observer who remembers, branch_on_intervention for the split on every shot) are used as primary and mixin. The mismatch is declared here rather than hidden.
evidence: ledger rules: 'Quantum immortality: death is refused unless observed'
waif-loop-canon: joined worlds backpropagate; they were running before he arrives

semanticReview.note: The retired letter index (J, T, M, C, with + and - tines) is mapped to the numbered splits of the compiled chart: J = split 10 (the crash), T = split 78 (the shot before she arrives), M = split 114 (the shot at her encouragement), C = split 184 (the last shot). Older charts and images may still carry the letter index.

The compiled chart lists scenes 202, 220, 238 and 256 inside the family world's lane, while the ledger has Marie and Jack killed in the siege and surviving only in the final pass. The siege and the seventh-chamber scene are placed here in the world where he died, following the ledger and the loop-canon note that the siege is off his thread. This placement needs Stephen to settle it.
evidence: waif-loop-canon references/bens-story-engine.md: 'ELSEWHEN in *3 (NOT his thread): padded room #158, siege #235-256'

semanticReview.note: The red-light pass at the end of the film is treated here as the family world, following the loop-canon note that the closing picture is the family world with a cruel man behind the wheel. The ledger reads the same scenes as a final pass that is calm from the opening out. Whether they are one world or two is not settled by either document.
evidence: waif-loop-canon: 'the red-light ending (p117-118 #277-278) is *F: family safe, cruel Ben behind the wheel'

semanticReview.note: The last shot is placed at scene 184 on the compiled chart but shown at page 113, scene 266 in the film's own order. Whether the chart's split 184 and the shot at #266 are the same act shown twice, or two separate shots, is not stated. Nothing here asserts they are duplicates.

The correspondence and attractor links between worlds are our reading of a film that shows the same beats recurring, not rules the script states. They are declared so that a reader can disagree with them.
evidence: ledger rules: 'The carousel: Waif retains memory across iterations'

semanticReview.note: Scenes the compiled chart places as beats without any note in the ledger (16, 31, 61, 85, 92, 99, 106, 128, 141, 154, 167, 202, 220, 238) are not encoded as events: there is no note to carry, and inventing one would be invention. What the chart says about them is their scene number and their world, and that is all.

The unseen passes are encoded as worlds that keep running after his death, not as repeats of one world. The loop canon is explicit that there is no rewind: what reads as a start-over is the film following the half that survived. Nothing here uses the word reset, and no reset event is declared.

The woman's own graph (the carousel: she dies, she dies, she dies, with one pass in which she lives) and the before-lives graph that belongs to the man who wrote the book are separate graphs. They are deferred, not dropped: they are not encoded as worlds or events here.
evidence: waif-loop-canon: 'Separate namespaces: Waif's graph W1, W2...; before-lives/Preston B1, B2... (separate graph, deferred not dropped)'

semanticReview.note: The crash splits the world in two, but only one half is ever shown. This world is declared because the split is declared; it has no events because the film has none for it.
evidence: bens-story.universes.json splits.10: 'THE CRASH - THE WORLDS SPLIT'

semanticReview.note: The three worlds he crosses into are encoded as pre-existing parallel worlds joined by a traveller, not as branches of his own. Earlier they were branches with no parent and no fork event, marked draft — which asserted a fork whose point was merely unknown. The film asserts the opposite: these worlds were running before he arrived and keep running after he leaves. Each shot still forks his own world (b_78, b_114, b_184 carry the half where he dies); the surviving thread does not continue in either half but joins a world already under way. Fork and join are now separate claims: forksFrom for descent, joinsInto for entry, with preExisting on the world and originWorldRef on the arrival. What remains DRAFT is whether the joined worlds are drawn from a fixed set the passes cycle through, or a fresh world each time; the encoding commits to neither.
evidence: waif-loop-canon: 'joined worlds backpropagate; they were running before he arrives'
world descriptions: 'already living before Ben arrives in it', 'it keeps running after he leaves it'

semanticReview.note: Four things the script leaves open are encoded as open, not answered: how many passes there have been; whether the man in the last pass remembers any of them; who the man in the corner office was when she jumped; and how she was taught to do what she does, which is only ever a padded room and a book with no explanation.

The figures who attack the house in the siege, described in the ledger as the Mother and the Woman in White, are not encoded as agents: the script does not say who they are. They appear inside the siege note and nowhere else. The pale figures are encoded because the script keeps them and names what they need.
evidence: ledger: 'SIEGE ... Mother + Woman in White attack'
ledger: 'The Others: pale-fire entities that need to be observed to exist'
